_README: DTS Error Grid straight-line border coordinates.
Source: Klonoff DC et al. 'The Diabetes Technology Society Error Grid and Trend
Accuracy Matrix for Glucose Monitors.' J Diabetes Sci Technol 2024;18(6):1346-1361.
DOI 10.1177/19322968241275701 -- Supplemental Appendix 2.
The grid is not trademarked and is in the public domain.
TO USE: copy this file to exp/dts_boundaries.json, replace every vertex list
below with the published coordinates, and delete the _TODO keys. Then run
python -m exp.dts_grid --selftest
and diff the printed zone table against https://www.diabetestechnology.org/dtseg/
FORMAT
Each vertex is [reference_glucose, monitor_glucose] in mg/dL, listed in
increasing reference order along the border.
'upper' borders lie ABOVE the identity line (monitor reads high -- the riskier
side, so these sit closer to the diagonal).
'lower' borders lie BELOW it (monitor reads low).
A point is in zone B if it is outside the AB border, C if outside BC, and so on;
the outermost border it clears wins.
Omit a border entirely if the published grid does not define it on that side
(for example the Parkes Type 1 grid has no zone E below the diagonal).
The placeholder numbers below are the PARKES TYPE 1 borders, present only so the
file parses and the plumbing can be exercised. They are NOT the DTS grid.
Reporting them as DTS numbers would be wrong.
